items.claim: The prohibition-plus-motive unit at 23:17-18 and its verbatim refrain link to 24:13-14 are both byte-confirmed, and the seam on both sides is clean.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.23.18's tail וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת is byte-identical (collate.py tier=byte) to oshb:Prov.24.14's tail וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת; the row correctly treats this as texture, never a boundary driver for either row. Neighbor verses 23:16 (closing the prior father's-joy address) and 23:19 (a fresh vocative reopening) share no root with 23:17-18, so both boundaries hold.

items.claim: The 23:19 vocative beni is a genuine E-1-corrected inventory site distinct from 23:15, and the 19-21 unit's boundaries are clean on both sides.
items.evidence: Prov.23.19 appears in prov_device_inventory.json bni_address (22-verse corrected list); the quoted שְׁמַע אַתָּ֣ה בְנִ֣י byte-matches the oshb text. Neither 23:18's hope-clause nor 23:22's father-command shares a root with 23:19-21, so the reopened-address argument holds without an undisclosed cross-seam device.

items.claim: The rejected_alternative's premise that no root repeats across the gap to 23:24-25 is byte-false: the father root recurs in 23:22, 23:24, and 23:25.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.23.22 לְ֭אָבִיךָ, oshb:Prov.23.24 אֲבִ֣י (father of the righteous), and oshb:Prov.23.25 אָבִ֥יךָ all carry the same root (byte-verified, collate.py tier=byte); the stated ground for rejecting a wider father-themed grouping overstates the case. This does not itself overturn the standalone-verse boundary -- 23:23's unrelated commerce topic still interrupts continuity -- but the row's specific claim needed qualification rather than a flat denial.

items.claim: The rationale's claim that 23:23 shares no vocabulary with the father's-joy couplet after it is byte-false: the wisdom root recurs in 23:23 and 23:24.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.23.23 חָכְמָ֖ה and oshb:Prov.23.24 חָ֝כָ֗ם share the root (byte-verified, collate.py tier=byte). The shared token is weak evidence on its own -- chokhmah-root vocabulary is book-wide common, 36 of 915 verses per the TOOLKIT hazard catalog -- so it does not overturn the single_proverb call, but the row's blanket phrasing is inaccurate and should have been narrowed or supported with that frequency digit rather than asserted as zero overlap.

items.claim: All four claimed ketiv/qere pairs at 23:24 and the qere-root recurrence opening 23:25 are byte-confirmed, and both boundaries of the cluster are clean.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json kq lists exactly 4 notes at Prov.23.24, matching the row's four named pairs (גול/גִּ֣יל, יגול/יָ֭גִיל, יולד/וְיוֹלֵ֥ד, וישמח/יִשְׂמַח) against the oshb byte text; the qere root recurs as the opening word יִֽשְׂמַח of 23:25 (byte-verified). Left seam (23:23, a distinct commerce maxim, no shared root) and right seam (23:26, a fresh vocative, no shared root) both hold.

items.claim: The 23:26 vocative beni and its ketiv/qere note are both byte-confirmed against the corrected inventory, and the 26-28 unit's boundaries are clean.
items.evidence: Prov.23.26 appears in prov_device_inventory.json bni_address (22-verse corrected list); the quoted תְּנָֽה בְנִ֣י לִבְּךָ֣ לִ֑י and the ketiv/qere תרצנה תִּצֹּֽרְנָה both byte-match the oshb text. Neither 23:25 (ending in the father/mother root) nor 23:29 (opening the wine poem's rhetorical list) shares a root with the vocative-plus-motive unit, so both seams hold.

items.claim: The span's own ketiv/qere inventory is incompletely disclosed: 23:29 carries a K/Q pair the row never mentions, though 23:31's is disclosed.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json kq lists 1 note at Prov.23.29, confirmed in the oshb byte text (מדונים מִדְיָנִ֨ים, tier=byte); the book strategy's own low-confidence-region guidance requires disclosure whenever a span touches a K/Q verse, and this span (23:29-35) touches two (23:29 and 23:31), but the row's evidence and device_notes name only 23:31's בכיס בַּכּ֣וֹס pair. The six-fold rhetorical-question count opening the span (word-bound לְמִ֨י, 6 occurrences in the verse) and the riddle-then-quoted-speech shape supporting the wisdom_poem call are themselves byte-confirmed and not in question here.

items.claim: The 24:1 ketiv/qere note and the envy-root recurrence at 24:19 are both byte-confirmed, and the row correctly treats the recurrence as texture rather than a boundary driver.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.24.1 וְאַל תתאו byte-matches the row's quoted pair; the envy root in 24:1's תְּ֭קַנֵּא recurs in 24:19's תְּ֝קַנֵּ֗א (byte-verified), and the row explicitly declines to widen the row on that basis, consistent with governance. Both the 23:35 left seam and the 24:3 right seam share no root with the pair.
